## Access-Control Requirement
The system manages advertising campaigns, creative review, and launch preparation.

The people involved are advertisers, account managers, brand safety reviewers, and campaign directors. One person may hold both the account manager and campaign director role at the same time.

The resources are campaigns and creatives. Every campaign records its advertiser, who prepared it, its budget, its contingency, its budget tier, its risk labels, its scheduled start, and its status.

Each requester carries a reviewer level.

Each request carries the current time, whether multi-factor authentication was used, whether the device is trusted, and whether the request is for an emergency launch.

A campaign director or an account manager may approve a campaign budget only while the campaign is in review when the campaign budget crosses the organization's money threshold and the budget tier is at or above the required level.

For campaigns whose budget does not cross the organization's money threshold, the review-status requirement for approving the budget does not apply.

For campaigns below the required budget tier, the review-status requirement for approving the budget does not apply.

A campaign director and an account manager must not approve a budget for a campaign that is not in review when the campaign budget crosses the organization's money threshold and the budget tier is at or above the required level.

A request by a campaign director to approve a budget that does not trip any prohibition above must be able to succeed.

## Access-Control Requirement
The system manages advertising campaigns and their launch readiness.

The people involved are advertisers, account managers, brand safety reviewers, and campaign directors. One person may hold both the account manager and the campaign director role at the same time.

The resources are campaigns and creatives. Every campaign records its advertiser, who prepared it, its budget, contingency, budget tier, risk labels, scheduled start, and status, and every creative records its campaign, who submitted it, its risk rating, content tags, and status.

Each requester carries a reviewer level.

Each request carries the current time, whether MFA was used, whether the device is trusted, and whether the launch is an emergency launch.

An account manager or campaign director may launch a campaign only after its budget is approved when the scheduled start time has not yet arrived.

Once the scheduled start time has arrived, the launch does not need to wait for budget approval.

An account manager or campaign director may launch a campaign only from a trusted device, and a launch request from an untrusted device is refused.

An account manager and a campaign director must not launch a campaign from an untrusted device.

A request by an account manager to launch a campaign that does not trip any prohibition above must be able to succeed.

## Access-Control Requirement
The system manages insurance policy underwriting and the binding of policies.

The people involved are underwriters, senior underwriters, underwriting managers, chief underwriters, and auditors. One person may hold both the underwriter and the senior underwriter role at the same time.

The resources are applications and policies. Every application records its assigned underwriter, its risk tier, its coverage lines, its segment, its premium, its product code, its exposure count, its status, and its effective date. Every policy records its application, who bound it, its premium, and its effective date.

Each request carries the current time, whether it comes from the corporate network, whether a catastrophe surge has been declared, and whether a staffing emergency has been declared.

In this workflow a policy is first bound and then an authority exception on the application is approved, and the exception step can see the application's status, its assigned underwriter, and its risk tier as recorded by the binding step.

An underwriter, a senior underwriter, or an underwriting manager may bind a policy only when their granted authority level covers the application's assessed risk tier, and an underwriter whose authority does not reach that tier may not bind it.

When an application's segment tag matches a monitored market segment, binding is subject to the monitored-segment controls, and an unmonitored segment is not.

When the annual premium is over the set monetary threshold, binding requires the elevated review, and for a premium at or below that threshold the standard review applies.

The authority exception must be adjudicated by the same underwriter assigned to handle the application, keeping one accountable owner across the file.

When the application's segment tag matches a segment under heightened scrutiny, the exception is subject to that heightened scrutiny, and an unflagged segment is not.

When the annual premium is over the threshold that mandates senior sign-off, the exception requires senior sign-off, and for a premium at or below that threshold no senior sign-off is mandated.

Neither a senior underwriter, an underwriting manager, nor a chief underwriter who is not the assigned underwriter may approve the application's exception.

A run through the workflow in which an underwriter whose authority covers the risk tier binds a policy and then, as the assigned underwriter, approves its exception, tripping no prohibition above, must be able to succeed.

Each requester carries an approval tier.

Each request carries the current time, daily cutoff, whether it is on the secure banking network, whether MFA was used, and whether an emergency was declared.

A treasury officer may release a wire after it has been verified.

A treasury officer must not release an unverified wire when the beneficiary is not on the account's screened allowlist and the request is not on the secure banking network.

When the beneficiary is on the account's screened allowlist, the treasury officer may release the wire even if it has not been verified.

When the request is on the secure banking network, the treasury officer may release the wire even if it has not been verified.
